title: Counsel – Settlement Team
posting_excerpt:
all aspects of complex product liability, toxic tort, and mass tort settlements from initial negotiations through final claim resolution and program closure.

The ideal candidate possesses extensive experience negotiating and implementing large-scale settlements involving thousands of claimants and has a deep understanding of contract drafting principles, claims administration, settlement allocation methodologies, lien resolution, data management, reporting obligations and compliance issues, and settlement fund governance.



ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

· Lead and support settlement negotiations in complex product liability, mass tort, toxic tort, and consumer product litigation matters.

· Help develop settlement structures and eligibility criteria.

· Serve as primary legal and operations lead, ensuring settlements are executed efficiently, accurately, and in accordance with all legal requirements.

· Work directly with plaintiffs’ counsel to negotiate, draft, review, and finalize all settlement-related documents, and to resolve any claimant disputes or appeals.

· Manage teams of nurse paralegals and other attorneys to review and assess the qualification and categorization of incoming claims.

· Perform data analysis across claims, such as monitoring values and identifying trends within a tort (e.g., for individual firms and claim groups) and across a settlement.

· Oversee all aspects of settlement implementation and claims administration, including workflow and quality assurance.



EXPERIENCE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES REQUIRED

· Juris Doctor (JD) degree from an accredited law school.

· Candidate must be active and in good standing with the local state Bar, or be eligible to waive in.

· Minimum of 8 years of significant and substantive experience practicing law, with a focus on mass torts in the drug, medical device and/or consumer products area(s), including at least three years of litigation practice at a law firm.

· Claims resolution experience, preferably with a focus on pharmaceutical products, medical devices, or consumer health or consumer-facing products.

· Detail-oriented with ability to simultaneously manage multiple teams and work streams.

· Familiarity with matter management systems (e.g., Case Manager Pro), claims administration platforms, and AI-enabled claim review platforms preferred.

· Experience drafting, reviewing and/or directly negotiating settlement documents, and a deep understanding of contracting principles generally.

· Strong problem-solving, project management, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

· The ideal candidate will also be highly motivated to be part of an active settlement practice, demonstrate initiative, an ability to assume responsibility for client matters, as well as the interpersonal skills to work well as part of a large, collaborative team.



WORKING CONDITIONS

1. Normal law office environment with little exposure to excessive noise, dust, temperature, and the like.

2. Must have the ability to work under pressure and multi-task.



The Counsel must be able to perform all essential job duties and responsibilities of this position with minimal supervision, satisfactorily and as outlined, with or without reasonable accommodation. Reasonable accommodation requests may be accommodated, absent undue firm hardship.

This job description is intended to describe the general requirements of this position. As such, it is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of job duties or responsibilities required in this job. Subject to firm needs, duties and responsibilities of this position may change at any time, on a temporary or permanent basis, and with or without notice.

title: Legislative Counsel
posting_excerpt:
he regulatory landscape around gig economy platforms, marketplace operators, and labor practices continues to evolve rapidly, the Legislative and Labor Team needs a skilled lawyer to analyze emerging requirements, build compliance frameworks, and shape the regulatory conversation before it shapes Instacart. Without this role, gaps in legal analysis and compliance strategy could create operational risk across multiple areas of the business. A year from now, Instacart will have stronger legal frameworks in place, clearer compliance strategies across regulatory domains, and a more coordinated voice in the cross-industry conversations that define the rules of the road for the gig economy.

What you'll cook up in your first year

- Cross-functional regulatory responses are coordinated with clarity: Policy and Government Affairs, Operations, Product, and Communications teams have a consistent, well-analyzed legal perspective on legislative matters affecting Instacart's operations.

- A comprehensive review of legislation impacting gig economy participants, marketplaces, retailers, and consumers is complete, with actionable legal guidance delivered to business partners to drive compliant operations.

- Legal frameworks and compliance best practices for meeting legislative and regulatory mandates are developed and documented, giving the company a foundation to navigate evolving requirements with confidence.

- Instacart's relationships with external counsel, trade associations, and industry partners are actively managed, with cross-industry initiatives underway that contribute to shaping the regulatory conversation in favor of gig economy innovation.

- Expertise in emerging areas of law relevant to Instacart's business is built and shared internally, ensuring the team is prepared to respond to new legal challenges as they arise.

The secret ingredients we're looking for

Must-have pantry staples (Minimum Qualifications)

- Juris Doctor (JD) degree.

- 3+ years of experience practicing law.

- Demonstrated ability to synthesize, analyze, and provide precise legal advice in response to legislative updates.

- Experience working with legislative bodies, government agencies, or regulatory matters.

- Proven success in supporting compliance initiatives and executing legal frameworks.

- Understanding of legislative processes and the regulatory landscape.

Optional garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)

- Experience with legislative or regulatory strategy.

- Familiarity with issues facing marketplace platform companies, gig economy platform companies, or similarly highly regulated businesses

#LI-Remote

Instacart provides highly market-competitive compensation and benefits in each location where our employees work. This role is remote and the base pay range for a successful candidate is dependent on their permanent work location. Please review our Flex First remote work policy here.

Offers may vary based on many factors, such as candidate experience and skills required for the role. Additionally, this role is eligible for a new hire equity grant as well as annual refresh grants. Please read more about our benefits offerings here.

title: Senior Counsel (Claims)
location: Chicago, IL, US; Dallas, TX, US; Downers Grove, IL, US; Nashville, TN, US; St. Louis, MO, US
posting_excerpt:
About You: 

We are looking for a service-oriented Attorney to join our team in our Downers Grove, IL office. The Senior Counsel (Claims) is primarily responsible for analyzing and helping resolve pre-litigation disputes, overseeing litigated and arbitrated claims, and partnering with senior attorneys and business leaders on claims handling and risk management strategies. This position also requires 10-15% transactional work, primarily negotiating owner and subcontractor agreements. 

A Day in the Life: 

- Collaborate with other members of the legal team located in our offices across the U.S. to address pre-claim disputes and manage litigated and arbitrated claims, including payment disputes, mechanic’s liens, safety incidents, subcontractor performance and licensing issues, and day-to-day project management issues.

- Partner with senior attorneys, project managers, and business leaders to understand business objectives in addressing and resolving claims.

- Implement enterprise-wide claims management and litigation best practices.

- Collaborate with members of the Safety, HR, and Finance teams to identify business risks and strategies for mitigation.

- Manage outside counsel and collaborate with insurance industry partners.

- Manage and present substantive reports on claims-related data.

- Remain informed of new laws, regulations, judicial opinions, and industry trends affecting the enterprise.

- Multi-task in a deadline-driven environment.

Necessary Qualifications: 

- Licensed attorney with 5-plus years of litigation experience.

- Experience in a construction organization, construction-focused law firm, or large law firm preferred, including substantive familiarity with standard Owner contracts, subcontracts, and mechanic’s lien processes.

- First- and second-chair trial and arbitration experience preferred.

- Strong oral and written communication skills, strategic and business acumen, and conflict resolution skills.

- Flexible, with effective and timely communication skills.

- 1-week paid volunteer leave each year

- 100% charitable match

- Medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage

- 100% paid 12-week maternity leave
